messages.content: Write a job posting for a senior backend engineer at a mid-sized fintech company. Around 250 words.

**Senior Backend Engineer**
[Company] — [City], or remote within US timezones

We move money for roughly 400,000 small businesses. Payments, ledgers, reconciliation, and a compliance surface that gets bigger every quarter. There are about 180 of us, 45 in engineering.

The role is on the payments platform team — seven engineers today. Go and Python services on Postgres, running in AWS, with Kafka wherever durability matters. What we've worked on lately: rebuilding the ledger into proper double-entry, pulling settlement from overnight to same-day, and unwinding a card processor integration someone rushed in 2021.

What we're looking for:

- Six or more years building backend services that other people rely on
- Financial data experience, or any domain where a missing cent counts as a bug instead of a rounding error
- Appetite to own a system end to end — the design, the on-call, and the postmortem after it breaks
- The ability to turn down a scope, in writing, with reasons

Nice to have, not required: payments specifics (ACH, card networks, ISO 8583), or time spent inside a regulated environment.

What you get: $180k–$225k plus equity, health coverage starting day one, on-call one week in seven with pages that are actually tracked, and a codebase with tests in it.

What we won't pretend: there's legacy here, and some of it is ugly. Plan on about a third of your time paying it down.

To apply, write us a short note about something you built and what you'd change about it today. No cover letter template.

Bracketed fields need your details; headcount, stack, and salary band are placeholders to swap for real numbers.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.
